newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends down on long liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended down sharply on Tuesday, with investors diverting funds to the more active stock market, traders said.
The key October contract ended at limit-down of 2,240 yuan ($269) per tonne, down 60 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 2,080. December fell 100 to 2,080 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell sharply to 1,900 tonnes from 12,700.
Traders said investors continued to offset their positions and had lost interest in trading.
"Some investors continued to liquidate long positions after heavy liquidation on Monday," one trader said.
Traders said open interest decreased sharply, which made it hard for the market to attract individuals looking to invest their money in the stock market.
The open interest of October was 1,370 lots and of December was 1,790. One lot is five tonnes.
Traders said trading would be slow in the next few days.
